paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, and I'm not going to joke about it. God lays out the charges against Oholah and Oholibah, the two sisters who stand for Samaria and Jerusalem, and the charges are serious. They gave themselves to idols, and they even went into His house on the very day they slaughtered their children for those idols (Ezekiel 23:37-39). The big idea is this: God takes unfaithfulness seriously because He takes His people seriously.

Look at what this passage says about sin that goes on and on. God speaks of her "who had grown old in adulteries" (Ezekiel 23:43). I think that's a picture of what happens when we keep drifting and call it normal. The sisters even took God's own incense and oil and set them on their luxury table (Ezekiel 23:41). So here is a question to ask yourself: what has God given me that I'm using for something else?

But notice where the passage ends. God says the sisters will bear the consequences of their sins, "Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD." (Ezekiel 23:49). He isn't wild or random here. He is the Lord, and what He says is true, whether people believe it or not. And this story isn't over, because there's more to what God says in Ezekiel. So, baker, keep your heart close to Him today, and hold nothing back from the One who is worth it.
